subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure on an affine plane spanned by an orthonormal frame (reuse of the accepted cbr_cipi_affine_plane_measure)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → Euclid P) (a : Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ w → Measure.map (fun z : Fin m → ℝ => a + ∑ i, z i • w i) volume = (μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ IsClosed {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) K < ∞) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) (ball a r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the selected node's supplied proof (the frame isometry, μHE[k] = volume on the frame space with Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, and toLp), carried out for the translated plane a + G. This statement is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbr_cipi_affine_plane_measure (accepted candidate 21dd628c), reused here with its identical frozen type; the proof below is the argument of that accepted declaration.
Notation: E_m := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) with the Euclidean norm; toLp := WithLp.toLp 2 : (Fin m → ℝ) → E_m, the identity on coordinates; G := span{w_1, …, w_m}, so S = {y : y − a ∈ G}.
1. (Norm identity.) Let c ∈ E_m. By orthonormality, ⟨Σ_i c_i w_i, Σ_l c_l w_l⟩ = Σ_{i,l} c_i c_l ⟨w_i, w_l⟩ = Σ_i c_i² (Orthonormal.inner_sum), and Σ_i c_i² = ‖c‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). So ‖Σ_i c_i w_i‖² = ‖c‖², and since both norms are ≥ 0, ‖Σ_i c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖.
2. (Isometry.) Define J' : E_m → ℝ^P, J'(u) := a + Σ_i u_i w_i. For u, u' ∈ E_m, J'(u) − J'(u') = Σ_i (u_i − u'_i) w_i. By step 1, dist(J'(u), J'(u')) = ‖u − u'‖ = dist(u, u'). So J' is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq), and in particular continuous.
3. (Range.) range J' = S. If y = J'(u), then y − a = Σ_i u_i w_i ∈ G, since each w_i ∈ G and G is a submodule. Conversely, if y − a ∈ G, then y − a = Σ_i c_i w_i for some c : Fin m → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, Fin m being finite), and y = a + Σ_i c_i w_i = J'(toLp c).
4. (Push-forward on the frame space.) On E_m, μHE[m] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For any isometry f, (μHE[m]).map f = μHE[m]⌞(range f) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). With steps 2–3 this gives (volume on E_m).map J' = H^m⌞S.
5. (Proof of (i).) As functions on Fin m → ℝ, J = J' ∘ toLp. toLp is measure preserving from volume on Fin m → ℝ to volume on E_m (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp), and J' is continuous, hence measurable. By Measure.map_map, (volume).map J = ((volume).map toLp).map J' = (volume on E_m).map J', which is H^m⌞S by step 4.
6. (Proof of (ii).) G is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). S is its preimage under the continuous map y ↦ y − a, so S is closed.
7. (Proof of (iii).) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by step 4 and Measure.map_apply (J' measurable), (H^m⌞S)(K) = volume(J'⁻¹(K)). An isometry defined on the complete space E_m is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), so J'⁻¹(K) is compact (IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage). Compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure (IsCompact.measure_lt_top), so (H^m⌞S)(K) < ∞.
8. (Proof of (iv).) Let r > 0. The open ball B_r(a) is Borel, so as in step 7, (H^m⌞S)(B_r(a)) = volume(J'⁻¹(B_r(a))). This preimage is open, because J' is continuous, and it contains 0, because J'(0) = a ∈ B_r(a). Lebesgue measure on E_m is an additive Haar measure, so it is positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpen.measure_pos; for m = 0, E_m is a single point of measure 1). Hence (H^m⌞S)(B_r(a)) > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: By orthonormality ‖Σ c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖, so J'(u) = a + Σ u_i w_i is an isometry of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), and its range is S (mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
volume.map J' = μHE[m]⌞S, from Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and μHE[m] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); composing with the measure-preserving toLp gives (i).
S is the preimage of the closed finite-dimensional subspace span(w) under y ↦ y − a, which gives (ii).
(H^m⌞S)(K) = volume(J'⁻¹K) < ∞, as J' is a closed embedding; (H^m⌞S)(B_r(a)) = volume(J'⁻¹B_r(a)) > 0, as this open set contains 0.

subproblems.title: Coordinate boxes in the span of an orthonormal frame have H^k-measure (2r)^k
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let g = (g_1, …, g_k) (g : Fin k → Euclid P) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P with span G := span{g_1, …, g_k}; H^k := μHE[k]. Then for every r > 0, the closed box {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i} and the open box {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| < r for all i} both have H^k-measure ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ g → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → μHE[k] {t | t ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) ∧ ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) t| ≤ r} = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * r) ^ k) ∧ μHE[k] {t | t ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) ∧ ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) t| < r} = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * r) ^ k)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the selected node's supplied proof. The push-forward identity they use (part (i), steps 1–3 there) is taken from the sibling affine_plane_measure at a = 0.
Notation: ι : (Fin k → ℝ) → ℝ^P, ι(u) := Σ_i u_i·g_i, where Fin k → ℝ carries its product Lebesgue measure volume and its sup norm ‖u‖ = max_i |u_i|. Fix r > 0, and write S≤ := {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i} and S< := {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| < r for all i}.
1. (Push-forward.) Apply the sibling affine_plane_measure (Submission.cbr_cipi_affine_plane_measure) with m = k, w = g and a = 0, and take its first conjunct: (volume).map (z ↦ 0 + Σ_i z_i g_i) = H^k⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ G}. Since 0 + x = x and y − 0 = y, the map is ι and the set is G. Hence (volume).map ι = H^k⌞G.
2. (Regularity.) ι is continuous, being a finite sum of the continuous maps u ↦ u_i·g_i, and hence measurable. G is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). For each i, t ↦ |⟨g_i, t⟩| is continuous.
3. (The boxes are Borel subsets of G.) S≤ ⊆ G and S< ⊆ G by definition. S≤ = G ∩ ⋂_i {t : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r} is an intersection of closed sets, hence closed and Borel. S< = G ∩ ⋂_i {t : |⟨g_i, t⟩| < r} is the intersection of the closed set G with finitely many open sets, hence Borel.
4. (Reduction to Lebesgue measure.) Let S be S≤ or S<. Then H^k(S) = H^k(S ∩ G) = (H^k⌞G)(S), by Measure.restrict_apply (S measurable) and S ∩ G = S (S ⊆ G). By step 1 this equals ((volume).map ι)(S), and by Measure.map_apply (ι and S measurable) it equals volume(ι⁻¹(S)).
5. (Coordinates of ι.) Let u : Fin k → ℝ. Then ι(u) ∈ G, because each g_l ∈ G and G is closed under sums and scalar multiples. For each i, ⟨g_i, ι(u)⟩ = Σ_l u_l ⟨g_i, g_l⟩ = u_i, because ⟨g_i, g_i⟩ = ‖g_i‖² = 1 and ⟨g_i, g_l⟩ = 0 for l ≠ i (orthonormality; Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype).
6. (Preimages are sup-norm balls.) By step 5, ι⁻¹(S≤) = {u : |u_i| ≤ r for all i} and ι⁻¹(S<) = {u : |u_i| < r for all i}. Since r ≥ 0, ‖u‖ ≤ r ⟺ |u_i| ≤ r for all i (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg, Real.norm_eq_abs), so ι⁻¹(S≤) = closedBall(0, r). Since r > 0, ‖u‖ < r ⟺ |u_i| < r for all i (pi_norm_lt_iff), so ι⁻¹(S<) = ball(0, r).
7. (Volumes.) Real.volume_pi_closedBall (r ≥ 0) and Real.volume_pi_ball (r > 0) give volume(closedBall(0, r)) = volume(ball(0, r)) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^{card(Fin k)}) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k) (Fintype.card_fin). With steps 4 and 6, H^k(S≤) = H^k(S<) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k). ∎
(For k = 0 the argument applies unchanged. Fin 0 → ℝ is a single point, ι ≡ 0, G = {0}, both boxes equal {0}, and both balls are the whole one-point space, of volume 1 = (2r)^0.)
proof_key_steps: affine_plane_measure at a = 0 gives (volume).map ι = H^k⌞G, where ι(u) = Σ u_i g_i.
Both boxes are Borel subsets of the closed subspace G, so H^k(S) = (H^k⌞G)(S) = volume(ι⁻¹ S).
ι(u) ∈ G and ⟨g_i, ι(u)⟩ = u_i by orthonormality, so the preimages are the sup-norm closedBall(0, r) and ball(0, r).
